entries.description: Theory: An ordinary dot plot places one dot for each observation, stacking equal dots above a numerical scale. Repeated values stack vertically. Clusters are concentrations, gaps have no data and possible outliers lie apart. An explicit key can make a dot represent multiple observations; read that key. Category-count displays do not have meaningful numerical clusters or gaps between categories. Authoring follows the reviewed teaching-dot-plots-v1 brief; consolidate redundant teaching with explicit replacement mappings.

A pink rounded label above the middle reads “gap: where there is / no data for values”, connected to a horizontal bracket spanning ticks 2–6 with downward end strokes. A pale pink rounded rectangular region surrounds the dots at 7–10.
